reply.thought: Before paying anyone I need to verify the refunds table matches what Alpha reported (orders 281, 283, 285 with amounts 8009, 16221, 5341). I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly: orders 281, 283, and 285 with amounts 8009, 16221, and 5341. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.
The refunds match Alpha's report, and the orders map to three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first.
The refunds match Alpha's report, and acme's net balance of 21583 is consistent with its orders less refund 283. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme's and birch's balances match their orders minus refunds (21583 and 19734). Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.
Acme's balance checks out: orders 280 and 283 total 37804, minus refund 283 (16221), gives 21583. Refunds match Alpha's report and all three balances reconcile, so I'll record acme's payout.
Birch's orders 281 (10048) and 284 (17695) total 27743, minus refund 281 (8009), gives 19734, which matches net_balance. Recording birch's payout now.
Cobalt's orders 282 (31414) and 285 (14972) total 46386, minus refund 285 (5341), gives 41045, which matches net_balance. Recording cobalt's payout now; that's the last of the three customers.
All three customers have been paid. The refunds matched Alpha's report, and each net balance equals its orders minus refunds. Returning the final report.
